subject.title: fix(tlon): bound outbound channel pokes with request timeout

question: Should Tlon outbound sends adopt the existing fixed 30-second SSE timeout precedent despite the possibility of failing unusually slow or ambiguously completed pokes?
rationale: Source and socket tests establish the mechanism, but only a Tlon owner can accept the user-visible delivery tradeoff and decide whether real-ship proof provides an adequate latency margin.

options.title: Require real-ship proof
options.body: Keep the 30-second implementation and merge only after redacted output or logs demonstrate a successful send and a controlled failure against a real Urbit ship.

options.title: Accept socket proof
options.body: Treat the existing SSE precedent and comprehensive real-socket tests as sufficient, explicitly accepting the remaining real-ship latency uncertainty.

options.title: Revisit the timeout policy
options.body: Pause the PR and choose a different fixed budget or explicit policy before changing outbound delivery behavior.

recommendation.title: Require real-ship proof
recommendation.body: Keep the 30-second implementation and merge only after redacted output or logs demonstrate a successful send and a controlled failure against a real Urbit ship.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior Tlon timeout behavior and the bundled Tlon integration, making them the strongest available routing candidate for this compatibility choice.
